name: Entity
title: Entities
body:
## Graph building blocks

An entity is an identifiable thing that people and agents need shared context about. Its stable ID is its identity; its name and documentation can change.

The graph has four building blocks:
- **Types** explain what a kind of entity or connection means and which properties it accepts.
- **Entities** are the actual projects, people, organizations, technologies, goals and documents. Each has a type, a stable ID and Markdown documentation.
- **Connections** are named, directed statements between two entities. They can carry notes, evidence and a status such as proposed.
- **Attachments** are files associated with an entity; their metadata and bytes have separate storage.

A type page explains a category. It is not an instance of that category. For example, Projects explains what a project is; a named research effort has its own page and can optionally link a Planning record.

## For agents

Discover the installed graph's types through `graph-type`, then read `graph-node` and `graph-edge` records. Use stable references and current revisions for changes. Read the relevant type documentation before creating context. A connection never grants permission to act. Advanced SemLang reasoning and analytics are future work.

name: Organization
title: Organizations
body:
## What an organization is

An organization is a company, institution or other identifiable group. Document what it does, its public references and its relationship to the work.

Business units are recorded separately when a team or department needs its own context. Organization and business-unit pages can connect to projects, people, agents and technologies.

## Example

Apple is an organization. Apple Health can have a `developed_by` connection to Apple. This does not imply that Apple owns projects which use Apple Health.

## For agents

Read the organization's documented scope and relevant connections. Graph membership is shared context, not an account permission, financial authorization or legal assertion.

## Canonical organization binding

The optional organization_id property records the exact authenticated platform organization ID this node represents within the current owner scope. A unique exact match can select its overview automatically. Missing or duplicate bindings require an explicit choice; never infer identity from a display name. This metadata does not grant access or authority. Standard data setup is add-only: existing installations need an explicit editor revision update to add this property to the Organization type and set the intended node; existing types and nodes are never silently rewritten.

properties.name: organization_id
properties.description: Optional exact platform organization ID represented by this Wiki Organization within the current owner scope. Consumers must require a unique match to the authenticated organization ID; display names are not identities. This binding grants no permissions. Existing installations require an explicit editor revision update; shared seed setup never overwrites an existing type or node.

name: BusinessUnit
title: Business Unit
body:
## Business units

A business unit is a team, department or area of work such as Life Sciences. Record its purpose, responsibilities and how its projects contribute to outcomes.

Connect projects with `belongs_to_unit` and people or agents through the projects they participate in. A unit can later support a community, but this record does not create community membership or permissions.

## For agents

Use the unit's documented scope to understand project priorities. Authority to change apps or run workflows is checked separately.

name: Project
title: Projects
body:
## What a project is

A project is a bounded effort toward an outcome. Use its page to explain the problem, desired result, scope, decisions and current evidence.

## What belongs on the page

Record readable Markdown documentation and connect the project to its business unit, human or agent participants, technology dependencies and goals. Distinguish proposed dependencies from operational integrations.

External projects can live directly in this Wiki without a Planning record. Connect them to their organization with `part_of` and document their goals, problems and dependencies through ordinary graph relationships. **Create/link project** offers **Document an external project** for this purpose. For work managed in Planning, create or select its canonical record and keep its verified `{installationId, type, id}` reference on the context page.

## Example

A health-data research project may have a proposed `uses` connection to a health platform. That connection documents intent; it does not prove a working connector.

## For agents

Read this context page and, when present, its linked Planning record before work. Standalone Project nodes can be created through the Wiki entity API or `graph.apply` without an app reference. Update the appropriate record through its app's entity operations, preserve any existing canonical reference and use the latest revision. Add decisions, evidence and progress to the documentation rather than claiming unsupported completion.

name: Person
title: People
body:
## What a person is

A person is a real human involved in the work. This page explains the People section; each actual person has a separate entity page.

## Identity and privacy

Two people may have the same name. Keep separate stable IDs and do not merge records using a name alone. Sources publish people through stable record references; Wiki notes remain independent of the source.

## For agents

Use the person's stable ID, documented responsibilities and project connections. A Person page is not proof of an authenticated account or consent to contact them. Confirm identity and permission through the relevant platform or connector before taking action.

name: Agent
title: Agent
body:
## Agents

An agent is a software participant, local or resident. Document its purpose, responsibilities, operating boundaries and links to projects.

This entity describes the agent; it does not provision a runtime, verify its identity or grant credentials. Use project participation and reporting connections as context.

## For agents

Read your assigned project, its business unit, relevant people, dependencies and goals before acting. Only use connectors and workflows permitted by the platform. Record evidence of progress and ask for required human decisions.

name: Technology
title: Technologies
body:
## What a technology is

A technology is software, a framework, a protocol, a service, hardware or another technical dependency worth documenting independently of a project.

Describe its purpose, important technical details, references, constraints and evidence of use. Use Product for a named software product and PhysicalComponent for a physical component when those descriptions fit.

## Example

Apple Health is a software product; HealthKit is a separate developer framework. A research project can document a proposed `uses` connection to Apple Health without asserting an operational HealthKit integration.

## For agents

Read the technology page and dependency evidence before building a connector or workflow. Preserve proposed versus observed status. A graph connection supplies context; execution and credentials come from the approved platform capabilities.

name: PhysicalComponent
title: Physical Component
body:
## Physical components

A physical part or component design relevant to a project: a mechanical part, a PCB, a bought (COTS) part or an assembly of parts. Document specifications, drawings, interfaces, evidence and practical constraints.

Designers, manufacturers and suppliers may be different organizations. Use `designed_by`, `manufactured_by` and `supplied_by` without assuming that one implies the others. Use `component_of` for the Product or assembly the part belongs to, `design_of` from its DesignArtifacts, and `includes_component` from each ProductRevision that pins it.

## For agents

Distinguish design intent, simulation, manufactured parts and measured physical behavior. Link evidence for compatibility and performance claims. Buy before build: record a bought part's manufacturer, MPN and datasheet so an equivalent can be found.

properties.name: kind
properties.description: mechanical, pcb, cots (bought as-is) or assembly.

properties.name: part_number
properties.description: Our own part number for this component.

properties.name: manufacturer
properties.description: Who makes it, for a bought part.

properties.name: mpn
properties.description: Manufacturer part number, for a bought part.

properties.name: datasheet
properties.description: URL of the datasheet or specification.

name: Goal
title: Goal
body:
## Goals

A goal describes a desired outcome. Document the result, accountable owner, target, time period and evidence that will determine progress.

Connect projects or participants using `pursues`. Connect a measurement definition using `measured_by` when the evaluation method is known.

## For agents

Use goals to choose useful work and report evidence. A goal page alone does not schedule a workflow or establish that the result has been achieved.

name: MetricDefinition
title: Metric Definition
body:
## Metric definitions

A metric definition explains how progress is measured: meaning, calculation, units, source, reporting interval and limitations.

It describes a measurement method. Actual observations and computed analytics are separate work; the existence of this page is not a measured result.

## For agents

Read the definition before interpreting a KPI. Report the period, source and evidence with any value. Future SemLang/Malloy integration may turn suitable definitions and observations into analytical queries.

properties.name: calculation
properties.description: How the value is calculated, including filters and exclusions.

properties.name: unit
properties.description: Unit of the measured value, for example percent, count or hours.

properties.name: source
properties.description: System or record set the observations come from.

properties.name: interval
properties.description: Reporting interval, for example weekly or calendar quarter.

name: Document
title: Document
body:
## Documents

A document is written context that needs its own stable identity, such as a decision, technical guide or evidence summary. Entity pages can also contain Markdown directly.

Use `documents` to connect a document to what it describes. A document about a project does not replace the canonical Planning project.

## For agents

Preserve provenance, references and authored conclusions. Separate evidence, assumptions and proposed decisions.

name: belongs_to_unit
title: belongs to unit
body:
Source project or unit belongs to the target business unit. No access grant is implied.

## For agents

Read this statement from its source entity to its target entity. Preserve the stable endpoint IDs and record supporting notes or evidence. Use proposed status when a connection has not been verified. The statement grants no execution permission.

properties.name: status
properties.description: Evidence status, for example proposed, documented, observed or retired.

properties.name: evidence
properties.description: Source URL or explanation supporting this statement; not proof of operational integration.

## For agents

Read this edge from the person or agent to the project or organization. Record responsibilities and evidence in the edge notes. Participation does not grant permissions.

name: measured_by
title: measured by
body:
## Measurement relationships

A goal, customer problem, project or organization is evaluated with a metric definition. A metric definition can in turn link to its measurement instrument or data source, such as a sensor platform.

## For agents

Read the metric definition for units, scope, targets and reporting periods. A target is not an observed value. A link to an instrument does not prove a working integration; distinguish intended sources from verified observations.

properties.name: status
properties.description: Evidence status, for example proposed, documented, observed or retired.

properties.name: evidence
properties.description: Source URL or explanation supporting this statement; not proof of operational integration.

name: documents
title: documents
body:
Source document describes target node. It does not replace that node or its canonical source.

## For agents

Read this statement from its source entity to its target entity. Preserve the stable endpoint IDs and record supporting notes or evidence. Use proposed status when a connection has not been verified. The statement grants no execution permission.

properties.name: status
properties.description: Evidence status, for example proposed, documented, observed or retired.

properties.name: evidence
properties.description: Source URL or explanation supporting this statement; not proof of operational integration.

name: part_of
title: part of
body:
## Organizational context

The source project is part of the target organization. Use this to group an organization’s projects without confusing the organization with an individual project.

## For agents

Follow this edge from a project to its organization for shared context. This relationship does not grant access or assert legal ownership.

name: Repository
title: Repositories
body: A version-control repository. Use one node for the whole repository and its URL in Website. Projects, technologies, software products and product revisions link through source_in. The relationship path identifies a monorepo directory; empty means the repository root. Its ref identifies a branch, tag or exact commit. Repository context grants no access.

name: source_in
title: source in
body: The source Project, Technology, Product or ProductRevision has code in the target Repository. Use the repository URL together with this relationship’s path and ref. A path scopes a monorepo directory; empty means the whole repository. Product revisions use an exact commit. This relationship is source location, not a dependency or access grant.

properties.name: path
properties.description: Repository-relative directory; empty for the whole repository.

properties.name: ref
properties.description: Branch, tag or commit used for browsing source.

name: collects_telemetry_from
title: collects telemetry from
body:
The source project collects telemetry produced by the target platform or project.

## For agents

Use this relationship to find the data source and the project responsible for collecting it. Consult their documentation for schemas, transport and deployment status.

name: Product
title: Products
body:
## Products

A product is an identifiable output of a project, such as a software application, sensor platform, consumer device or service. Keep its specifications, interfaces and usage documentation here. The project describes the work that creates and maintains it.

Connect the project to its product with `produces`. Connect a consuming project or product to another product with `uses`. For example, a sensor-development project produces a sensor platform, and a consumer product proposes using that platform.

## For agents

Keep project and product identities separate. Follow the producing project for work and ownership context. A produces or uses relationship records intent unless evidence establishes delivery or operational use.

name: produces
title: produces
body:
## Project outputs

The source project creates or maintains the target product. This separates the work from the output other projects and products can use.

## For agents

Follow this edge from project to product. Record proposed status for planned outputs; the relationship alone does not establish that a product has shipped or is operational.

properties.name: status
properties.description: Evidence status, for example proposed, documented, observed or retired.

properties.name: evidence
properties.description: Source URL or explanation supporting this statement; not proof of operational integration.

name: CustomerSegment
title: Customer segments
body:
## Customer segments

A group of prospective or existing customers with shared needs, such as commercial spaces with indoor plants or home plant owners. A segment is not an individual organization.

## For agents

Use `in_segment` to connect people or organizations to the segment, and `experiences` to connect it to shared customer problems. A proposed `customer_of` relationship describes an intended market, not a signed customer.

name: Problem
title: Customer problems
body:
## Customer problems

A need or difficulty experienced by customers. Keep one shared problem when several segments experience the same need. Document the desired outcome and gaps in current measurement.

## For agents

Use `experiences` from a customer or segment to this problem, `addresses` from a project or product to the problem, and `measured_by` to link relevant success metrics. A coverage metric such as monitored plants does not alone prove plant health or problem resolution.

name: customer_of
title: customer of
body:
The source person, organization or customer segment is a customer or prospective customer of the target provider organization or project.

## For agents

Direction is customer to provider. Use proposed status for target customers or hypotheses; never infer contracts, purchases or endorsements from this relationship.

properties.name: status
properties.description: Evidence status, for example proposed, documented, observed or retired.

properties.name: evidence
properties.description: Source URL or explanation supporting this statement; not proof of operational integration.

name: in_segment
title: in segment
body:
The source person or organization belongs to the target customer segment.

## For agents

Segment membership describes shared needs and is separate from an established customer relationship. Preserve proposed status when unvalidated.

properties.name: status
properties.description: Evidence status, for example proposed, documented, observed or retired.

properties.name: evidence
properties.description: Source URL or explanation supporting this statement; not proof of operational integration.

name: experiences
title: experiences
body:
The source customer or customer segment experiences the target problem.

## For agents

Reuse shared problem entities across segments. Record proposed status until customer research supports the problem statement.

properties.name: status
properties.description: Evidence status, for example proposed, documented, observed or retired.

properties.name: evidence
properties.description: Source URL or explanation supporting this statement; not proof of operational integration.

name: addresses
title: addresses
body:
The source project, product, organization or release aims to address the target customer problem.

## For agents

Follow the problem’s measured_by relationships for evaluation. Proposed solutions and monitoring coverage are not evidence that the customer problem has been solved.

properties.name: status
properties.description: Evidence status, for example proposed, documented, observed or retired.

properties.name: evidence
properties.description: Source URL or explanation supporting this statement; not proof of operational integration.

name: integrates_with
title: integrates with
body:
## Product integration

The source technology connects or is intended to connect with the target technology. This is separate from who develops either product.

## For agents

Use status and evidence to distinguish an intended integration from verified operational behavior. This relationship does not install a connector or grant access.

properties.name: status
properties.description: Evidence status, for example proposed, documented, observed or retired.

properties.name: evidence
properties.description: Source URL or explanation supporting this statement; not proof of operational integration.

name: Role
title: Roles
body:
## Roles

A reusable responsibility such as CEO, CPO, CFO, CTO or Senior Software Engineer. A role describes responsibilities; it is separate from the person or agent holding it and from the organization where it applies.

## For agents

Find RoleAssignment entities linked to this role through `assigns_role`. Do not infer permissions or runtime provisioning from the role name.

name: RoleAssignment
title: Role assignments
body:
## Role assignments

A role assignment joins one Person or Agent, one Role, and one organization or other work scope. Separate assignments allow one holder to have multiple roles and preserve organization-specific agent identities.

Use `assigned_to` for the holder, `assigns_role` for the role, and `scoped_to` for its organization. The holder and role are participant slots; scope stays an ordinary `scoped_to` connection because scopes such as boards are defined by other apps. Put business dates on the assignment's validity (from inclusive, until exclusive), never on its slot connections.

## For agents

Read all three relationships together. Missing links mean incomplete context. An assignment documents responsibility and does not grant application permissions, deploy a resident agent or configure reporting lines.

name: assigned_to
title: assigned to
body:
The source RoleAssignment is held by the target Person or Agent.

## For agents

Preserve the holder’s stable identity. Different organization-specific agents may share a display name but must remain separate entities.

name: assigns_role
title: assigns role
body:
The source RoleAssignment assigns the target Role.

## For agents

Read the assignment’s holder and scope to understand where this role applies. Multiple roles require separate assignments.

name: scoped_to
title: scoped to
body:
The source RoleAssignment or DecisionRecord applies within the target organization, business unit or project.

## For agents

Read the scope before using role or decision context. A title held in one organization does not carry over to another organization.

name: DecisionType
title: Decision types
body:
## Decision types

A named kind of decision, such as Approve Release. It describes what may be decided, not an approval of a particular release.

## For agents

Follow incoming `permits` relationships to authority definitions. Concrete DecisionRecords link here with `decision_type`. Execution permissions and enforcement remain outside this context graph.

name: AuthorityDefinition
title: Authority definitions
body:
## Authority definitions

A reusable definition of decision authority. Its `permits` relationships identify the decision types it covers.

## For agents

An AuthorityGrant points here with `defined_by`. Read the grant’s role and the holder’s RoleAssignment scope together. This record describes authority; it is not a platform permission.

name: AuthorityGrant
title: Authority grants
body:
## Authority grants

A grant gives a role the authority described by one AuthorityDefinition. Follow `has_authority_grant` from Role to grant, then `defined_by` to its definition and `permits` to DecisionType.

## Scope

A holder’s authority applies in the organization of their RoleAssignment. An unscoped or incomplete assignment does not establish scoped authority. Archived grants do not contribute current authority.

## For agents

This is documented decision authority, not executable authorization. Release workflows still require their own permissions and approval checks.

name: has_authority_grant
title: has authority grant
body:
The source Role holds the target AuthorityGrant.

## For agents

Combine the role’s grant with a holder’s explicit RoleAssignment scope. Never infer cross-organization authority from a shared role name.

name: defined_by
title: defined by
body:
The source AuthorityGrant is defined by the target AuthorityDefinition.

## For agents

Read the authority definition’s permitted DecisionTypes; the grant alone does not approve any concrete action.

name: permits
title: permits
body:
The source AuthorityDefinition permits the target DecisionType.

## For agents

This relationship documents a permitted kind of decision. It is not an actual decision, release approval or deployed permission check.

name: Offering
title: Offerings
body:
## Offerings

An offering packages and prices a product for customers. The product is the reusable thing; the offering describes what a customer can obtain and its commercial terms. Multiple offerings may package the same product differently.

Use `packages_product` to identify the product, `offered_by` for the provider, and `pays_for` from the customer to the offering. Omit an unknown price; zero means free, not unknown.

## For agents

Read pricing notes and the relationship status. A proposed paying-customer relationship is not an invoice, completed payment, contract or deployment.

## Pricing models

Inference may use cost_plus pricing: provider cost plus a markup. Resident-agent offerings may use role_based pricing, with priced_by_role edges carrying optional per-role prices. Missing rates remain unspecified; do not infer free usage.

properties.name: price
properties.description: Explicit price when known; omit if not specified.

properties.name: currency
properties.description: Currency code for the stated price.

properties.name: billing_interval
properties.description: One-time, monthly, usage-based or other stated interval.

properties.name: pricing_notes
properties.description: Commercial terms, scope and unresolved pricing details.

properties.name: pricing_model
properties.description: Commercial pricing basis, such as cost_plus or role_based.

properties.name: markup_percent
properties.description: Explicit percentage added to provider cost; omit when not specified.

name: packages_product
title: packages product
body:
The source Offering packages the target Product.

## For agents

The offering holds commercial terms; the product holds technical identity. Do not duplicate the product for each customer or price.

name: offered_by
title: offered by
body:
The source Offering is offered by the target organization.

## For agents

Offering a product does not imply manufacturing or designing it; follow those relationships separately.

name: pays_for
title: pays for
body:
The source customer organization or person pays or intends to pay for the target Offering.

## For agents

Use proposed status for a planned commercial relationship. Read the offering for package and pricing terms. This edge is not proof of a settled payment.

properties.name: status
properties.description: Evidence status, for example proposed, documented, observed or retired.

properties.name: evidence
properties.description: Source URL or explanation supporting this statement; not proof of operational integration.

name: priced_by_role
title: priced by role
body:
The source Offering has a pricing tier based on the target Role. Optional edge properties describe that role’s price and billing interval.

## For agents

This is a commercial rate relationship, not a role assignment or authority grant. An omitted price is unknown, not zero.

properties.name: price
properties.description: Explicit rate for this role; omit when unspecified.

properties.name: currency
properties.description: Currency for this role rate.

properties.name: billing_interval
properties.description: Billing interval or unit for this role rate.

name: DecisionRecord
title: Decision records
body: A concrete decision made by a person or agent. Record rationale, outcome, decision time and conditions in Markdown. Link decision_type, made_by, under_assignment and scoped_to. For release approval, scope to the exact ProductRevision, record its node revision and build identity, and supported_by the ReadinessAssessment. Approval, passing checks and deployment are separate facts. This records context, not executable authorization or a tamper-proof audit log; a current assignment does not prove historical authority.

properties.name: status
properties.description: Decision state, such as proposed, decided or superseded.

name: decision_type
title: decision type
body: The source DecisionRecord is an instance of the target DecisionType.

name: made_by
title: made by
body: The source DecisionRecord was made by the target Person or Agent.

name: under_assignment
title: under assignment
body: The source DecisionRecord was made in the capacity of the target RoleAssignment. Preserve this historical link if the assignment later ends.

name: establishes
title: establishes
body: The source DecisionRecord establishes the target goal. Read the decision rationale, organization scope and the goal’s measured_by links.

name: Activity
title: Activities
body:
## Activities

An identifiable practice, recurring pursuit or bounded activity in personal or organizational life: yoga practice, training, inspections or a team workshop. Repeated calendar entries may support one activity; each appointment need not become a separate activity.

## For agents

Separate the activity from its individual occurrences, preferences and goals. A scheduled activity does not establish attendance, enjoyment, success or a health condition. Connect people and organizations with participates_in, retaining evidence and uncertainty.

name: Asset
title: Assets
body:
## Assets

An identifiable resource that a person or organization may own, control or use, such as a home, vehicle, equipment or business property. PhysicalComponent describes a part or design; Asset captures the resource in a life or business context.

## For agents

Record ownership, use, value and financing as separate claims. A mortgage notice may suggest a property but does not prove legal ownership, address, market value or equity. Unknown values remain unknown. Personal and organizational assets use the same type.

name: FinancialObligation
title: Financial obligations
body:
## Financial obligations

An identifiable financial responsibility of a person or organization, such as a mortgage, loan, payable or recurring contractual obligation. It is distinct from its payment notices, individual transactions, financed asset and provider product.

## For agents

Use has_obligation from the responsible person or organization. Use secured_by only when evidence supports the collateral relationship. Do not infer a paid transaction, debt balance, interest rate, delinquency or financial distress from a scheduled payment notice. Amounts and dates require explicit supporting evidence.

name: Question
title: Questions
body:
## Questions

An individually identifiable unresolved question about an entity or relationship. Explain what is unknown, why the answer matters, and the evidence that raised it. It applies to personal and organizational knowledge.

## For agents

Link subjects with about. Keep questions separate from facts, goals and problems: asking about cost does not establish excessive cost. User answers can support new claims; retain the original evidence and do not silently overwrite authored knowledge.

properties.name: status
properties.description: Question lifecycle: open, answered or dismissed.

name: participates_in
title: participates in
body:
A Person or Organization participates or proposes participating in an Activity.

## For agents

Scheduled participation is distinct from observed attendance. Record proposed when only calendar evidence is available; do not infer enjoyment or a goal.

properties.name: status
properties.description: Evidence status: proposed, observed or user-confirmed. Publication alone is not confirmation.

properties.name: evidence
properties.description: Supporting source references and limits on the claim.

name: owns
title: owns
body:
A Person or Organization owns an Asset.

## For agents

Treat a candidate ownership claim as proposed until supported or confirmed. A payment notice alone does not establish title or ownership share. This relationship grants no authority.

properties.name: status
properties.description: Evidence status: proposed, observed or user-confirmed. Publication alone is not confirmation.

properties.name: evidence
properties.description: Supporting source references and limits on the claim.

name: has_obligation
title: has obligation
body:
A Person or Organization is responsible for a FinancialObligation.

## For agents

name: OutfitterUser
title: Outfitter users
body:
## Outfitter users

An Outfitter account: a member or an agent principal on an Outfitter host. Its key is `<host>/users:<id>`, set only by the platform, and it never changes. Link it to the Person or Agent it belongs to with `account_of`.

## For agents

An account is how Outfitter knows someone, not who they are. Describe the person on their Person page; an account grants nothing by itself.

name: OutfitterOrganization
title: Outfitter organizations

## Outfitter organizations

An Outfitter organization account on an Outfitter host. Its key is `<host>/organizations:<id>`, set only by the platform. Link it to the Organization it belongs to with `account_of`.

name: account_of
title: account of
body: The source account belongs to the target Person, Agent or Organization. One account belongs to one holder at a time; relationships grant no access.
